analysis:
Reviewed the supplied base-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 798-1628) and the file_changes patch. The only change is a documentation-only addition at head lines 2172-2184. It describes constrained-decode chaining for FlintNativeProtocolConstraint and FlintAnswerStopConstraint, a state-keyed device mask cache (maskCacheKey), and putting the RecursiveSI/flint-int4 catalog artifact on the automatic paged list, which starts it at legacy width 8 on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra. No code, config or deployment changes are in this batch, so no controls are altered directly.

Threat-model observations for later passes, not findings:
(1) The added doc claims the token stream is identical to unchained decode, because step N+1 is redrawn from retained logits when state changes. That correctness and determinism claim is unverified here. It would matter for T-007 and T-056 only if the underlying code diverged from the doc.
(2) The state-keyed mask cache holds only constraint state, not prompt-derived content. It looks cross-request safe, but the actual implementation was not supplied. It could touch T-028 (residual GPU data) or T-041 (cross-tenant timing) only if the cache key embedded tenant or prompt data, which the doc says it does not.
(3) Paged-allowlist promotion of flint-int4 raises concurrency to 8 on larger chips. This is a resource and availability matter (T-010, T-029). Per the existing doc, memory admission and posture gating (Low Power Mode and thermal pressure fallback) still apply, and the width catalogs remain empty.

The base excerpts cover pre-existing documented behavior (deadlines, MTP, SSD prefix cache, vision caps). They are not modified by this PR, so nothing is re-reported. Source code implementing the Flint chaining is outside the supplied evidence, so the doc's accuracy is unverified; this is recorded as a coverage limit.
